text:
About 60 percent of the world's population lived in low and lower-middle income countries in 1997. I'm recalling that figure, not checking it, and the $1230 cutoff doesn't match the Bank's usual 1997 thresholds. The team note is wrong: in 1997 China and India were still low-income countries, so they sit below the $1230 line. Their roughly 2 billion people are the main reason the share is so large.

CONFIDENCE: 40
